_comment: Starter rules. Copy to rules.json and edit. Keep patterns HIGH-SIGNAL: a false deny costs more trust than a missed catch, because a guard that cries wolf gets switched off — and then it protects nothing. Grow this file from real mistakes, not imagined ones.
_targets: command = Bash tool_input.command | path = file_path | content = text being written | action = command+path (NOT content — use this for protected-resource rules so writing docs ABOUT them doesn't trip the guard) | any = everything
_decisions: deny = hard block, for irreversible or externally-consequential actions. ask = routed to the human, for risky-but-legitimate ones.

rules.reason: Recursive force-delete. Confirm the exact target before running it.
'git add -A/.' sweeps in unrelated work and races any background process that commits. Stage explicit paths instead.
Force-push rewrites published history. Confirm the branch, and that nobody else's work is on it. (--force-with-lease is deliberately exempt.)
Destroys uncommitted work irreversibly. Confirm, or stash to a named branch first.
Deleting a managed secret is irreversible and silently breaks live services. Back the value up and grep for usages first.
This directory is air-gapped by policy — its contents never leave this machine. Replace SENSITIVE_DIR_NAME with your own protected directory names.
This data is under a preservation obligation. Deleting or moving it is never correct.

rules.pattern: (MIT License|Apache License|Permission is hereby granted, free of charge)
rules.reason: This tree holds proprietary code. Never scaffold a permissive license into it — and fix the README prose too, not just the LICENSE file.
